主要内容: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) announced on April 15, 2014, the appointment of David J. Gottesman as deputy chief litigation counsel in the Division of Enforcement. Gottesman joined the SEC in 2004 and was promoted to a supervisory role in the trial unit in 2011. He has litigated cases involving financial and accounting fraud, insider trading, market manipulation, investment company and adviser fraud, offering fraud, and registration violations. Andrew J. Ceresney, director of the SEC’s Division of Enforcement, praised Gottesman’s legal expertise and leadership. Matthew C. Solomon, chief litigation counsel, highlighted Gottesman’s trial acumen and success in challenging cases. Gottesman has led several jury trials, including a two-week trial against Hayes-Lemmerz executives and a financial crisis case against Charles Schwab & Co. He also contributed to an $18 million settlement with Philip A. Falcone. Gottesman received his bachelor’s and law degrees from the University of Minnesota and previously worked at Rosenthal and Schanfield, P.C., and the U.S. Department of Justice.
